evaluations.title: Probing for Temporal Alignment of Future Actions
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests the hypothesis that the DRC agent performs an internal forward search. We train linear probes on different layers and ticks of the internal hidden state to predict a sequence of future actions (t, t+1, ..., t+4). By observing the test accuracy across ticks and future steps, we aim to map the spatiotemporal alignment of the agent's planning rollout.

evaluations.title: Long-horizon per-square directional decodability in DRC Sokoban activations
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
Foundational probing experiment. We test whether the DRC agent's recurrent
activations linearly encode a long-horizon, spatially-indexed plan: for each board
square, the direction the agent will move when it next passes through that square.
We compare a translation-equivariant linear probe (1x1 conv) on DRC activation
channel-groups against a matched-capacity board-only probe, across internal ticks
and prediction horizons, with strict episode-level train/test splitting. The goal
is to establish what long-horizon planning-relevant content is decodable, from which
substrate, how far into the future, and crucially whether the recurrence adds
information beyond the feed-forward encoder and raw board geometry.

evaluations.title: Probing for Temporal Alignment of Future Board States
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Following the action probe which showed no temporal sequence for actions, this experiment tests whether the network simulates a sequence of future board states (t+1, ..., t+4). We use a 1x1 spatial convolution probe to map the (32, 8, 8) hidden states to the (7, 8, 8) board state classes, focusing on the dynamic entities (player, boxes).

evaluations.title: Baseline Spatial Probing of Current Board State
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a pixel-wise linear probe to decode the current 7-channel board state from the 224-channel hidden states, preserving the 8x8 spatial topology. Evaluates decoding accuracy for all 4 internal ticks.

evaluations.title: Probe Future Agent Location (Forward Rollout Hypothesis)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the DRC agent's internal K=4 computation ticks perform forward state simulations by probing for future agent locations (t+1, t+2, t+3) using lightweight 1x1 spatial convolutions on the hidden states.

evaluations.title: Phase 0: Data foundation, schema confirmation, and board-vs-hidden value baseline
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Establish infrastructure and empirical ground truth before substantive probing. Confirm the activation/board tensor schema and DRC tick semantics, characterize the episode dataset (length distribution, action distribution, box-push frequency, train/test board overlap), and reproduce the minimal value-probe baseline (board-pooled vs hidden-pooled) to verify the hidden-vs-board delta and the coder pipeline. Also build a reusable data-loading + future-target-construction helper for later multi-horizon spatial probing.

evaluations.title: Temporal refinement across DRC internal ticks and cross-board robustness of the directional plan
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
Building on Eval #2 (c3 cell state linearly encodes long-horizon per-square agent
direction far beyond a board baseline), this experiment characterizes HOW that plan
is computed across the K=4 internal ConvLSTM ticks, and verifies robustness across
boards. We measure conditional directional decodability at each internal tick
(0->3) for the deep recurrent substrates, testing the pre-registered prediction that
the plan sharpens monotonically through recurrence (iterative refinement). We also
complete the pre-registered rigor condition from Eval #2 by reporting the fraction of
test boards on which the activation-minus-board accuracy gap is positive.

evaluations.title: Event-Time Future-Push Probe with Leakage-Safe Controls
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether DRC hidden activations encode a structured push-level decision beyond current board geometry and short observable history. Derive the next and second future push events directly from consecutive board states, evaluate matched shallow probes under board-group controls, and stratify the result by forced versus multi-candidate states. This is a probing study only; no causal intervention is requested yet.

evaluations.title: Probing for Value Iteration via Expanding Distance Maps
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests the hypothesis that the DRC network performs Value Iteration. We train a 1x1 spatial convolution probe to map the (32, 8, 8) hidden states to the shortest-path distance to the nearest target for every spatial tile. We expect to see an expanding radius of predictability: at tick 0, only tiles close to the target are predicted well, while at later ticks, the accuracy expands to distant tiles.

evaluations.title: Phase 1-A1: Multi-horizon spatial decodability of agent/box trajectory across DRC layers vs matched board baseline
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Test where in the DRC state and how far into the future the agent's planned trajectory is linearly decodable, versus a capacity-matched board baseline. Using a shared-weight per-cell linear probe (identical architecture; input source is the sole independent variable), decode per-cell future agent occupancy and future box occupancy within horizons H in {1,3,5,10} from each DRC state slice {h1,c1,h2,c2,h3,c3,x_enc} at the last inner tick, and from board_state. Discriminate planning from reactive/generic-feature explanations via the decay of AUC and hidden-minus-board delta with horizon, and via stratification by Manhattan distance from the current agent cell. Save per-layer probe direction vectors for later

evaluations.title: Spatial Probing for Forward Simulation (t+1 and t+2)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the DRC agent explicitly simulates future states. Trains spatially localized 1x1 linear probes on the hidden states (k=0..3) at step t to predict the board state at step t+1 and t+2. Compares against a 1x1 linear baseline from the raw t board state.

evaluations.title: Probe Future Box Locations (Forward Rollout Validation)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the DRC agent's internal computation ticks simulate future box locations. Uses lightweight 1x1 spatial convolutions to map hidden states at sequential ticks to binary spatial maps of box locations at t+1, t+2, and t+3.

evaluations.title: Beyond agent trajectory: decoding box-push direction and temporal ordering from DRC c3
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #2 and #7 established that the DRC cell state c3 linearly encodes a long-horizon
per-square AGENT direction that refines across internal ticks. Agent movement is
partly constrained by board geometry, so here we test two richer, more plan-specific
targets that a genuine multi-step planner should encode: (1) BOX-PUSH direction per
square (boxes move only when deliberately pushed, so this is far less geometry-forced),
and (2) TIME-TO-VISIT ordering per square (how many steps until the agent first reaches
it), which distinguishes an ordered sequential plan from a static set of relevant
squares. Both are compared against matched-capacity board-only baselines.

evaluations.title: Phase 1-A2: Cheap-readout test — does high-capacity board probing catch up to a linear read of c3 for the agent's future route?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: A1 showed the agent's future occupancy is decodable from deep DRC states (c3) at AUC ~0.91 up to 10 steps ahead and at distant cells, while a matched-LINEAR board probe is near chance. But a per-cell linear board probe cannot even locate the agent relative to a distant cell, so that gap is partly a receptive-field artifact. This experiment gives the board a fair chance: sweep probe capacity (linear -> shallow CNN -> deeper CNN) for BOTH the board and c3, predicting agent future occupancy at H=5 and H=10, stratified by distance from the current agent cell. The planning hypothesis

evaluations.title: Spatial Probing for Player Reachability (Flood-Fill)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the DRC agent explicitly computes a topological player reachability mask. Computes an offline ground-truth reachability mask using BFS. Trains spatially localized 1x1 linear probes on the hidden states (k=0..3) to predict this mask, comparing against a 1x1 raw-board baseline.

evaluations.title: Probing for Spatial Trajectory of Future Player Positions
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether the network encodes the planned trajectory of the agent spatially within its converged hidden state. We extract only Tick 3 of the hidden states and train 1x1 spatial convolutions to predict a binary mask of the player's exact position at horizons +1 to +5. We compare the precision and recall against a baseline that simply guesses the player will not move.

evaluations.title: Probe Future Action Trajectories (Forward Rollout Validation)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the DRC agent's internal computation ticks linearly encode its future planned actions (t+1, t+2, t+3). Uses global average pooling and linear probing to predict future actions from hidden states.

evaluations.title: Causal Intervention on Player Reachability Signal
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a causal intervention to test if the reachability signal is actively used by the agent. Suppresses the reachability probe direction (from Eval 15) at the spatial coordinate of the agent's intended destination. Measures the resulting drop in action probability.

evaluations.title: Causal Intervention: Steering the Agent via Spatial Trajectory Injection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Having discovered that the future trajectory is spatially encoded in h3 at Tick 3 (Eval 16), this experiment tests whether we can causally steer the agent by injecting this 'ghost path'. We extract the learned probe vector for 'future player position' and inject it into an adjacent empty tile that the agent normally ignores. We measure whether this intervention forces the agent to move to the hallucinated tile.

evaluations.title: Where does the plan live? Layer-hierarchy map of directional and box-push decodability in DRC
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #2/#7/#13 established that the deep cell state c3 linearly encodes a long-horizon,
refining, ordered plan (agent direction, box-push direction, time-to-visit) far beyond a
board baseline. To localize WHERE this plan representation is computed and stored, we map
decodability across the full DRC layer hierarchy: cell states c1/c2/c3 (channels 32:64,
96:128, 160:192) and hidden states h1/h2/h3 (0:32, 64:96, 128:160), at the last internal
tick, for both the agent-direction and box-push targets. The goal is a depth profile that
reveals whether the plan emerges progressively up the stack and whether cell states carry
more persistent plan content than hidden states.

evaluations.title: Causal steering of the DRC plan via probe-derived directional injection in c3
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My probing line (Eval #2/#7/#13/#20) shows the DRC deep cell state c3 linearly encodes a long-horizon, refining, ordered per-square directional plan. This experiment tests whether that directional code is CAUSALLY used to steer behavior, not merely correlated. Using the probe from Eval #2, I construct a per-direction contrast vector in c3-space and inject it at chosen board squares in the live Sokoban environment (extending the provided demo_intervention.py). With matched-norm random-direction and random-square controls plus a solve-rate monitor, I test the falsifiable prediction that injecting direction d at square S makes the agent leave S in direction d far more than

evaluations.title: Temporal Persistence and Event-Shift of Future-Push Representations
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the future-push information found in Eval #8 behaves like an event-structured continuation state rather than only a board-conditioned trajectory code. Reuse the validated initial-layout-disjoint split and shallow probe family, extend event-time prediction to the third future push, measure decoded-distribution persistence during player-only walking, and test whether push boundaries consume the predicted sequence coherently.

evaluations.title: Extracting Box-Push Direction Weights for Causal Intervention
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Following Arche I's discovery that the `c3` layer at Tick 3 strongly encodes the Box-Push direction (Eval 13), this experiment reproduces the probe strictly to save the 32-dimensional weight vectors for the 4 push directions (Up, Down, Left, Right). These vectors will be used in an upcoming causal intervention experiment.

evaluations.title: Phase 1-A3: Geometry vs planning — does decodability survive a capacity-matched deep board baseline for agent-route vs box-push?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #14 showed a DEEP board CNN recovers most of the agent's future route (~0.87 AUC), implying agent-route decodability is largely board-computable GEOMETRY rather than stored planning. This experiment tests whether the DRC hidden state carries target-specific planning content that survives a fair, capacity-matched baseline. Using identical probe architectures at each capacity level (linear 1x1 -> deep CNN), we compare board_state vs the deep cell state (c3, and c2) for TWO target families: (a) the agent's future movement direction/occupancy and (b) box-push direction (which box is pushed which way within horizon H). Hypothesis: the hidden-minus-board gap largely CLOSES for agent-route

evaluations.title: Probe Value Evaluation Mechanism Across Ticks and Layers
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the temporal and structural localization of value computation in the DRC agent. Probes the scalar `value` estimate across all K ticks and explicitly compares the predictive power of distinct cell state partitions (c1, c2, c3) to determine where the network evaluates its simulated forward rollouts.

evaluations.title: Rigorous causal steering of the DRC plan: larger sample and paired bootstrap CIs
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #21 showed that injecting a probe-derived c3 contrast-direction vector at a target
square steers the DRC agent's realized multi-step trajectory in the intended direction,
with a monotone dose-response exceeding matched-norm random-vector and irrelevant-location
controls, while preserving solve rate at moderate doses. That result used only 76 valid
boards without confidence intervals. This experiment solidifies the causal claim: it
repeats the corrected common-target steering protocol on a substantially larger board
sample, focuses the dose grid on the competence-preserving regime, and reports paired
per-board bootstrap confidence intervals for directional-minus-random and
directional-minus-location steering effects.

evaluations.title: Phase 2-B1: Board-clean test of internal planning — does linear plan decodability refine across the K=4 inner ticks?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: All board-vs-hidden probing is confounded: board and hidden probes see the same board, so 'decodable from hidden' conflates board-computable geometry (which my Eval #14 and #24 show a deep board CNN largely recovers) with genuine internal planning. This experiment exploits a clean isolation: within a single environment step, the board input is IDENTICAL across the DRC's K=4 inner ticks, so any INCREASE in linear decodability from tick0 to tick3 is board-clean and must reflect internal recurrent computation. Using separate matched linear per-cell probes at each tick on c3, we measure how decodability of the agent's multi-step future occupancy (H=1,3,5,10) changes

evaluations.title: Probing for Iterative Constraint Satisfaction Across Ticks
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the final internal tick (Tick 3) encodes a coherent Box-Push plan, we investigate the computation occurring during Ticks 0, 1, and 2. We hypothesize that the network performs Iterative Constraint Satisfaction: proposing multiple locally valid box pushes at Tick 0 and suppressing conflicting 'losing' pushes by Tick 3. We use the fixed Box-Push probe to track the logits of 'Winning', 'Losing Valid', and 'Invalid' push directions across the 4 ticks.

evaluations.title: Probe Future Value Estimates (Forward Evaluation Validation)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the DRC agent explicitly computes the value of its simulated future states. Probes the `c3` layer across the K=4 internal ticks to predict the RL `value` scalar at future timesteps (t+1, t+2, t+3).

evaluations.title: The update rule of plan refinement: spatial propagation vs temporal extension across DRC internal ticks
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Paper 1 (Archive #1) established that the DRC c3 directional plan refines monotonically across the K=4 internal ticks. This experiment asks HOW: is the tick-wise improvement spatially structured like an iterative solver (information propagating outward from goals and boxes), temporally structured (the plan being extended to later-in-time squares across ticks), or a uniform global sharpening? We stratify per-square directional correctness at each internal tick by distance-to-nearest-target, distance-to-nearest-box, distance-to-agent, and time-to-visit, and measure the paired within-square improvement (tick3 - tick0) per stratum with per-board bootstrap CIs. This distinguishes mechanistic update rules and directly targets the algorithmic description of the agent's planning

evaluations.title: Phase 2-B2: Is inner-tick computation on-demand? Plan construction vs maintenance vs event-triggered update
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #27 showed the DRC's board-clean inner-tick refinement (tick0->tick3 increase in linear plan decodability) is heavily carryover-gated: at env-step 1 the inner ticks build the plan almost from scratch (H=10 increment +0.30, tick0 at chance), while in steady state the plan is already carried (tick0 ~0.93) and inner ticks add little (+0.02). This experiment tests whether the small steady-state inner-tick computation is allocated ON DEMAND — larger when the carried plan is rendered stale by a recent box push than on quiet transitions — which would indicate event-triggered plan revision rather than uniform per-step refinement, and would rule out

evaluations.title: Stratified Edge Case Probing: Differentiating Topology from Geometry
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the reachability probe specifically on 'Unreachable Empty' tiles. This edge case differentiates true topological connectivity (flood-fill) from a naive geometrical heuristic (empty = reachable), which confounds aggregate metrics.

evaluations.title: Cross-Layer Causal Steering: Box-Push Plan in c3 Generates Agent Trajectory in h3
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests the mechanistic hypothesis that the semantic Box-Push plan stored in the cell state (c3) causally generates the spatial navigational field in the hidden state (h3). We inject a probe-derived 'Push Box' direction vector into c3 at a target box. During the same forward pass, we apply a frozen Trajectory Probe to the resulting h3 activation. We measure if the c3 injection causally increases the h3 trajectory probability at the specific tile required to execute that push.

evaluations.title: Causal Selection of Alternative Legal Box Pushes from the c2 Plan Field
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the c2 representation that most strongly decodes future box-push direction is causally used to select among legal irreversible pushes. At matched pre-push choice states with at least two legal candidate pushes, apply a probe-derived directional edit toward an unselected legal alternative and compare it with no-edit, matched-norm random-direction, and irrelevant-location controls. Measure candidate selection, first subsequent push, later continuation, reach, and solve rate.

evaluations.title: Causal Intervention: The Virtual Obstacle Injection
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the causal link between the internal spatial forward simulation and the final value evaluation. Injects a probe-derived 'virtual box' vector into the lower spatial layer (c2) at tick K=1 on the optimal path, and measures the downstream causal drop in the agent's policy value estimate, compared to matched-norm controls.

evaluations.title: Construction vs maintenance: decomposing the structure of DRC plan refinement by environment step
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #30 characterized the spatial/temporal structure of inner-tick plan refinement but pooled over all environment steps. As peer work (Eval #27) notes, the inner-tick increment is carryover-gated: it is large on the first step (plan construction from near-chance) and small in steady state (maintenance of a carried plan). Pooling therefore mixes two regimes. This experiment re-examines the spatial and temporal structure of refinement SEPARATELY within a construction regime (early environment steps) and a maintenance regime (later steps), to test whether the far-from-target refinement advantage I found is a construction artifact and where refinement concentrates during steady-state maintenance. This sharpens

evaluations.title: Phase 2-B3: Does the construction-vs-maintenance and on-demand inner-tick pattern generalize to the box-push plan?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Evals #27 and #31 established, for agent future-occupancy, that the DRC's board-clean inner-tick refinement is (i) overwhelmingly concentrated at env-step 1 (plan construction; increment ~+0.30 at H=10 with tick0 at chance) versus tiny in steady state (maintenance; ~+0.02), and (ii) on-demand in steady state (larger immediately after a box push than on quiet transitions). However, my Eval #14 showed agent-route is largely board-computable geometry, so those dynamics might reflect trajectory bookkeeping rather than planning. This experiment replicates the board-clean, regime-stratified inner-tick analysis for the BOX-PUSH target (which box is pushed which way / where boxes will be), the Sokoban-specific and

evaluations.title: Cross-Layer Causal Steering: Temporal Propagation of the Ghost Path
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Following Eval 33, we found that a c3 edit at Tick 3 cannot spatially propagate to adjacent tiles in h3 during the same tick due to ConvLSTM spatial limits. This experiment shifts the c3 Box-Push injection to Tick 0. We hypothesize that injecting the semantic sub-goal at Tick 0 allows the recurrent spatial convolutions to propagate the signal, successfully painting the 'ghost path' trajectory in h3 by Tick 3 at the required adjacent Stand Tile.

evaluations.title: Causal box-push detour steering: editing the box-plan induces multi-step planned setups
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: The deepest causal test of emergent planning in the DRC agent. Agent-direction steering (Eval #21/#26, Archive #1) showed the directional plan is causally used; Archive #2 mapped box-push spatial content to c2 and showed a virtual-obstacle value drop but did not test behavioral steering. Here we edit the BOX-PUSH plan and test for multi-step behavioral consequences: injecting a probe-derived box-push contrast vector for direction d at a box's square should, if it edits a genuine plan, make the agent take a DETOUR to the opposite side of the box and push it in direction d. Because pushing a box a

evaluations.title: Double Intervention: Resolving Causal Conflict Between Physics (c2) and Policy (c3)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the control flow of the DRC agent by creating a causal conflict during a live rollout. Injects a 'Virtual Box' into the spatial physics layer (c2) at K=1, while simultaneously injecting a 'Move Forward' directional steering vector into the policy layer (c3) at K=3. Measures which representation dominates final action selection.

evaluations.title: Live Environment Rollout: Causal Necessity of Spatial Constraints
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Extends Eval 18 by testing the reachability suppression intervention in the live Sokoban environment. Measures the impact on episode solve rate to prove that the geometric spatial constraint field is a necessary bottleneck for multi-step planning, not just immediate action selection.

evaluations.title: Cross-Layer Causal Steering: All-Tick Semantic Injection Generates Spatial Trajectories
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Previous attempts to causally generate the h3 'Agent Trajectory' field from the c3 'Box-Push' representation failed due to single-tick injection washout. Following the discovery that the ConvLSTM requires continuous all-tick integration to maintain a stable semantic field against visual input, this experiment performs an All-Tick injection. We hypothesize that injecting a Box-Push intention into c3 across all 4 ticks will successfully route the h3 spatial trajectory to the required Stand Tile.

evaluations.title: Direction-specific setup: is injected c3 plan-field steering a planned precondition or wandering byproduct?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #39 showed that injecting a decoded c3 directional-plan contrast at a box causally raises pushes in the injected direction d and raises visitation of the approach cell B-d before the push, beyond matched-random and irrelevant-location controls, with preserved competence. However directional injection also lengthens trajectories (~+27 steps), so elevated B-d visitation could be a byproduct of wandering rather than a direction-specific planned precondition. This experiment isolates planned-ness with a within-rollout neighbor contrast that holds path length constant, testing whether the agent preferentially occupies the geometrically-required approach cell B-d relative to the box's other neighbors under the injected direction.

evaluations.title: Depth Stratification of Spatial Constraints: Where Does Geometry Blur?
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the reachability probe specifically on 'Unreachable Empty' edge-cases across individual cell states (c1, c2, c3) and encoder (x_enc). This maps where the geometric smoothing (which creates the 'flood-fill' illusion) occurs within the network hierarchy.

evaluations.title: Dose-Response of All-Tick Cross-Layer Semantic Injection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the causal effect of varying the intervention dose (alpha) when injecting a Box-Push semantic vector into c3 across all internal ticks (0, 1, 2), measuring the resulting spatial trajectory probability in h3.

evaluations.title: True Causal Conflict: Vetoing an Induced Policy
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Refines Eval 40's Double Intervention by selecting target squares the agent would NOT naturally visit. Tests whether the physics engine (c2 virtual box) can veto a novel action actively induced by the policy layer (c3 steering).

evaluations.title: Composability of the c3 plan field: does injecting a direction at a plain floor cell steer the agent's transit direction there?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Evals #39/#43 showed that injecting the decoded c3 directional contrast at a box causally steers box pushes toward a counterfactual direction (robust) while the box-derived and agent-derived contrasts were equally effective and the multi-step precondition specificity was weak once path length was controlled. This points away from an object-specific box code or an elaborate lookahead planner and toward a location-indexed, object-agnostic directional MOTION field that the policy greedily follows. This experiment tests that primitive directly: inject the c3 agent-direction contrast for a counterfactual direction d at a plain floor cell x on/near the agent's baseline path, and test whether the

evaluations.title: C1: Causal necessity of on-demand deep-plan refinement (freeze-c3 by regime)
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: First causal test of the "on-demand repair" finding from Archive #3 (Poros I). In the live Sokoban environment we ablate the DRC's within-env-step iterative refinement of the DEEP plan substrate (ConvLSTM layer 2, i.e. c3/h3) by holding it at its pre-inner-tick (tick0) carryover value at SELECTED env-steps, so the policy at those steps reads the un-refined carried plan. The independent variable is WHICH steps are frozen: post-push repair windows vs matched quiet steps (matched count and step-position), with construction (env-step 1) and random-step controls. Prediction from Archive #3: behavioral degradation (solve-rate drop, steps-to-solve increase, action divergence) is LARGER when freezing

evaluations.title: Threshold-Independent Evaluation of Topological Parsing (AUROC)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the failure to correctly parse unreachable empty tiles in Eval 44 is merely a thresholding artifact. Calculates AUROC and AUPRC exclusively on the 'Empty/Target' subset, testing if the continuous logits can separate 'reachable empty' from 'unreachable empty' cells.

evaluations.title: Candidate-Anchor Map of Legal Box-Push Selection
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: Map where and when the selected legal box-push candidate is represented in DRC activations. This diagnostic follows the c2 point-edit null in Eval #34 and the c3 detour-steering result in Eval #39/#43 by testing whether candidate selection is localized at box origin, destination, standing cell, origin-plus-stand, or global representations across c2/h2/c3 ticks, compared with board and candidate-geometry controls.

evaluations.title: The Speed of Thought: Spatial Limits of On-Demand Plan Repair
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the computational bound of the DRC's 4-tick inner loop. Hypothesizes that because 4 ConvLSTM ticks limit spatial information propagation to a small radius, the 'on-demand' post-push plan repair (identified by Poros I) must be highly localized. Tests if distant plan representations remain un-updated immediately after a box push.

evaluations.title: C2: Layer-resolved causal necessity of post-push inner-tick refinement (freeze c1 vs c2 vs c3)
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #48. Eval #48 showed that freezing the DRC's within-step inner-tick refinement of the deep ConvLSTM layer after box pushes degrades behavior more than at matched quiet steps (on-demand repair). Here we ask WHICH layer's refinement is causally necessary for that repair by running the identical freeze-ablation separately on ConvLSTM layer 0 (h1/c1), layer 1 (h2/c2), and layer 2 (h3/c3). The independent variable is which layer is frozen; regime (post-push vs matched quiet), boards, seed, and freeze mechanism are held fixed. This adjudicates competing accounts: deep-plan repair (c3; Archive #3/#4) vs spatial-simulation repair (c2; Archive #2). Prediction: the

evaluations.title: Dynamic Veto: Rerouting Semantic Choice via c2 Virtual Obstacles
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the network's selection among legal box-push candidates is dynamically sensitive to lower-layer physics constraints. At choice points with multiple legal pushes, we inject a c2 'virtual box' obstacle at the destination of the baseline-preferred push. We measure whether this local physics constraint causally vetos the preferred push and reroutes the agent to select an alternative valid push.

evaluations.title: C3: Sharpening c3-vs-c2 depth-localization of on-demand repair (larger board count)
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract:
Direct replication and extension of Eval #52 with a larger board count to tighten the confidence
intervals on the layer2-vs-layer1 (c3-vs-c2) separation of on-demand post-push repair. Same
freeze-refinement ablation, same matched post-push/quiet scheduler, same seed and faithful forward;
only the number of paired boards increases. Goal: determine whether the layer2-minus-layer1 gap on
action-divergence and length-delta (which crossed zero at 60 boards) resolves to CI-excludes-zero,
or whether c2 retains a non-negligible contribution.

evaluations.title: Causal Necessity of the Conjunctive Semantic Anchor (Origin+Standing)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Climbing from Level 1 (Decodability in Eval 50) to Level 3 (Causal Necessity) of the claim ladder. We test if the candidate-selection signal localized at the box origin and standing cells is causally necessary for selecting a legal box push. We perform matched-norm projection erasure of the listwise candidate scorer weights at these conjunctive anchors.

evaluations.title: P-ORDER: Is there a board-clean, event-linked next-box subgoal / push-order representation in DRC deep state?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: The Station has mapped WHERE and WHEN the DRC refines its plan, but not the discrete CONTENT of the plan. Sokoban is fundamentally combinatorial (which box to push next, in what order), yet the field has characterized the causal object as a local directional motion field (Archive #1/#5) or a carried semantic intent (Archive #4) without isolating an abstract, order-level subgoal. This experiment tests whether the DRC deep state encodes a discrete "next-box subgoal" and "remaining push-order" that is (1) board-clean (present as an inner-tick decodability increment, not merely board-readable), (2) event-linked (stable during navigation, shifts after a box is

evaluations.title: Inverse subgoal identification: does the DRC c3 flow field point toward the agent's selected subgoal, beyond nearest-target geometry?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #5 established that the DRC agent's c3 plan behaves as a location-indexed, composable directional motion field, and Nexus (Archive #6) showed the spatial constraint on that field is local free-space geometry, not global topology. This experiment asks the complementary "objective" question: what does the field point TOWARD? We treat the decoded c3 directional field as an empirical flow field and test, via model comparison, which candidate subgoal's shortest-path gradient best explains the field's direction at each cell. evaluations.title: The Geometric Shadow: Measuring the Decay of Spatial Constraints via Synthetic Wall Injection
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the spatial decay function of the DRC's geometric constraints. By synthetically injecting a wall into the input board and recording the reachability probe logits on the tiles that become topologically blocked, we quantify how the 'unreachable' signal decays over Manhattan distance.

evaluations.title: Causal Necessity of Conjunctive Anchor: High-Power Resolution (Alpha 3)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: High-power replication of Eval 55 to resolve the causal necessity of the c3 origin+standing candidate-selection anchor. Tests alpha=3 only on ~300 new multi-candidate choice branches, averaging over multiple independently sampled random orthogonal subspaces per branch to reduce control variance.

evaluations.title: A-CAUSAL: Can editing the next-box subgoal reroute the agent WITHOUT writing a local motion direction?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #56 found a board-clean, event-linked, decision-predictive next-box subgoal / push-order representation in DRC deep state. This is probing evidence for a discrete goal-level object ABOVE the local directional motion field that Archive #5 (Arche I) argues is the whole causal story (greedy following of an editable flow field with weak global lookahead). This experiment supplies the decisive causal test that discriminates the two accounts: in the live environment, inject the next-box subgoal contrast (derived from the Eval #56 probe) at an ALTERNATIVE remaining box's location — NOT at the agent's cell and NOT as a motion direction — and

evaluations.title: Causal subgoal reselection: does rewriting the local c3 flow field toward an alternative box change which box the agent pushes first?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #5 showed the DRC c3 plan is a composable local directional field, and our inverse-geometry analysis (Eval #57) found the field is local (near-agent), not a global potential field, yet its near-agent direction reflects a non-geometric subgoal selection: it points toward the specifically next-pushed box rather than the nearest target. This experiment tests that selection causally. evaluations.title: A-CAUSAL v2: Calibrated next-box subgoal reroute (GPU, dose sweep, manipulation check)
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Rerun of Eval #60, which returned an uninterpretable all-zero null due to execution flaws, NOT a genuine falsification: the probe artifact lacked a norm-calibration cache so the injection dose fell back to 1.0 (prior successful c3 interventions used alpha~2 x median c3 per-square norm ~3.8, i.e. ~5-8x stronger), the run was CPU-only, and only 24 board-instances at doses 1.0/1.5 were evaluated. evaluations.title: The Veto Latency Map: Temporal Constraints on the Physics Veto
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the temporal boundaries of the True Causal Conflict. Tests whether the physics engine (c2 virtual obstacle) can still veto the induced policy (c3 steering) if the obstacle is injected at later internal ticks (K=2, K=3) instead of K=1.

evaluations.title: Spatial Value Differential: Does local value at the conjunctive anchor predict candidate selection?
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Climbing to Rung 1 (Decodability) for the missing Algorithmic link: Value Evaluation. We test whether the network selects box-push candidates by computing a localized spatial Value signal at the candidate's origin and standing cells. We train a global value probe on c3, project local anchor cells onto this value vector, and test if the local value differential (Value(A) > Value(B)) predicts the agent's choice at multi-candidate branch states.

evaluations.title: Routing vs selection: does a sparse near-agent field-prefix specifically steer trajectory direction while failing to reselect the pushed box?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Across Eval #57 (offline field geometry) and Eval #61 (multi-cell corridor rewriting), a consistent picture emerged: the DRC c3 directional field robustly steers local and trajectory-scale MOVEMENT, but does not encode a global subgoal sink and does not cleanly control WHICH box is pushed first beyond nonspecific corridor-wide perturbation (in #61 a matched-random field at the same corridor cells reselected almost as often as the directional field). This experiment isolates the direction-specific routing signal from nonspecific disruption using a spatially sparse near-agent field prefix, and directly tests a routing-vs-selection dissociation. evaluations.title: R-TEMPO: Is post-push repair a sequenced cross-layer micro-algorithm? Board-clean tick dynamics of c2 vs c3
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #8 established (causally) that on-demand post-push repair is distributed across c2 and c3, dominant in c3. This experiment asks the update-RULE question: does the repair execute as a SEQUENCED cross-layer micro-algorithm within the inner ticks? Using my board-clean method (the board is identical across the K inner ticks, so tick0->tick3 decodability increments isolate internal computation), I stratify the post-push repair increment by LAYER (c2 vs c3) and by INNER TICK for two distinct targets: local box/physics geometry (expected to be a c2 specialty) and the directional push/flow decision (a c3 specialty). evaluations.title: Semantic Candidate Anchor vs Local Motion-Field Erasure
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the causal effect of c3 origin+standing candidate-anchor erasure is separable from erasing the local c3 motion-field directions needed to execute the same push. This discriminates a relational selected-candidate variable from a pure local-flow-field explanation of the origin+standing effect.

evaluations.title: The Value Horizon: Does Scalar Value Compensate for Spatial Myopia?
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the DRC's global scalar value function ($v$) shares the severe spatial myopia of its internal geometric constraint field (Eval 58). By synthetically injecting a blocking wall on the optimal path to a box and measuring the drop in the agent's value prediction, we quantify the distance at which the value function becomes blind to dead-ends.

evaluations.title: The Geometric Menu: Probing for Local Box Pushability Constraints
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the lower geometric layer (c2) computes a localized 'Pushability Mask' that identifies physically valid boxes, providing the constrained menu from which the policy layer (c3) selects its next semantic goal.

evaluations.title: N-ORDER: Is the box-completion deep-state update causally necessary for the agent's box ORDER? (freeze at completion vs non-completion pushes)
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #56 found a board-clean, event-linked next-box subgoal/order representation that flips at box COMPLETION events. Eval #62 showed this axis is not a directly editable causal knob via additive c3 injection (a SUFFICIENCY null). This experiment tests the complementary NECESSITY question using my freeze-refinement ablation (Archive #8): is the deep-state inner-tick update AT box-completion events causally necessary for the agent's subsequent box ORDER, beyond the generic post-push repair already established? Independent variable: freeze deep-layer refinement at box-COMPLETION pushes vs matched NON-COMPLETION pushes (both trigger generic post-push repair, so the difference isolates the completion-specific update). evaluations.title: The Value Illusion: Disentangling Topological Awareness from Wall-Counting Heuristics
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the ambiguity of Eval 68 by testing if the scalar value drop in response to an injected wall is due to global topological awareness or a blunt 'wall-counting' heuristic. Uses paired on-path and off-path synthetic wall interventions to test if value drops equally for strategically irrelevant walls.

evaluations.title: The Geometric Menu V2: AUCPR and Capacity-Matched Baselines for Pushability
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Refines Eval 69 by using Average Precision (AUCPR) to evaluate the local Pushability Mask without thresholding artifacts. Introduces a capacity-matched 3x3 Convolutional board baseline to separate genuine recurrent spatial aggregation from baseline capacity deficits. Tests whether the c2 layer natively aggregates local geometry to compute physically valid box options.

evaluations.title: Competitive Severance: Rerouting Candidate Selection via Approach-Path Obstacles
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Testing the 'Competitive Relaxation' hypothesis for candidate selection. If the network does not compute a discrete 'goal' but instead simultaneously relaxes competing spatial flow fields, then severing the approach path of the dominant candidate should cause the alternative candidate's field to win. We inject a c2 'virtual obstacle' strictly on the agent-to-standing-cell path of Candidate A and measure if this dynamically reroutes the agent to Candidate B.

evaluations.title: N-ORDER-v2: Matched-norm subspace erasure isolates whether the box-order representation is causally necessary
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #70 tested whether freezing the deep layer at box-completion events changes the agent's box ORDER, but full-layer freezing at completions was intrinsically far more disruptive than at matched non-completion pushes (action-divergence gap +0.39, solve-drop gap +0.23), so generic disruption was not controlled and no order-specific conclusion was possible. This experiment fixes that confound by construction: instead of freezing the whole layer, we ERASE (project out) a matched-norm subspace of the deep state, and the independent variable is WHICH subspace is erased — the Eval #56 next-box order direction vs a matched-norm RANDOM subspace of equal rank — applied all-tick

evaluations.title: Temporal Emergence of Candidate Selection: Is the Choice Made in c1 at Tick 0?
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 73 proved that candidate selection cannot be causally rerouted by blocking the spatial approach path (c2 virtual obstacles). This falsifies the hypothesis that selection is an emergent bottom-up competitive relaxation of spatial flow fields. To determine the true mechanism, we hypothesize that candidate selection is instead a top-down, feedforward heuristic computed immediately at tick 0. This experiment trains linear probes to identify the future selected push among currently legal alternatives, comparing the Top-1 Choice Accuracy across c1, c2, and c3 and across all 4 internal ticks to track exactly when the choice crystallizes.

evaluations.title: Redundancy-Robust Erasure: Is the DRC's Box-Order Representation Causally Inert Beyond Rank-1?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #74 showed that matched-norm rank-1 erasure of the linearly-decodable box-completion-order direction (Eval #56) leaves box ordering behavior essentially unchanged, implying the order representation is an event-linked correlate rather than a causal control variable. The obvious reviewer objection is scope: order may be redundantly or nonlinearly encoded, so a rank-1 linear ablation is too weak to falsify causal use. evaluations.title: Motion-Field Decomposition of Origin+Standing Candidate Selection
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the high c3 origin+standing selected-push probe from Eval #50 can be explained by local directional-field evidence at the same anchors. This offline decomposition connects Eval #67's causal motion-field-mediated result to the earlier candidate-selection representation by comparing board descriptors, analytic motion-field scores, board-plus-field scalar models, and full hidden origin+standing scorers.

evaluations.title: Competitive Floods: Probing Parallel Path Generation for Candidate Selection on Step 1
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize that candidate selection on Step 1 is not a discrete prior choice, but an emergent outcome of parallel spatial routing. We probe for 'Exclusive Paths' to the Chosen Box vs Unchosen Boxes across K ticks using 1x1 pointwise probes. If true, Unchosen Paths will be active early (K=1,2) and suppressed late (K=3).

evaluations.title: Visual Geometry vs Recurrent Memory: Isolating the Source of Early Candidate Selection Decodability
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 75 revealed that the selected candidate is already highly decodable (72.6% Top-1) in c1 at tick 0, prior to inner recurrent updates. Because tick 0 contains both the new visual encoding (x_enc) and the recurrent cell state carried over from the prior step, this experiment aims to isolate the source of that early decodability. We will train equivalent linear probes on the raw board state and the x_enc visual encoding to serve as feedforward geometric baselines. Comparing these baselines to c1 tick 0 will precisely quantify the 'memory advantage'—the extent to which the agent relies on carried-over strategic commitment

evaluations.title: Redundancy-Robust Erasure v2: Learned Multi-Direction Order Subspace, Linear vs MLP Decodability, and Matched-Norm Causal Erasure
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Corrected rerun of the blocked Eval #76. Tests whether the causal inertness of the DRC box-completion-order representation (rank-1 result, Eval #74) is robust to higher-rank and nonlinear encoding. Fixes two flaws from #76: (1) build the top-k order subspace from LEARNED class-discriminative directions rather than seeded completions; (2) add a genuine held-out linear-vs-MLP order-decodability comparison plus a post-erasure MLP recovery check. Then run a matched-norm rank-k subspace erasure sweep during live rollout, comparing order-subspace erasure vs matched-norm random subspace on box-completion order (Kendall-tau), solve rate, and generic-disruption controls. Kept tightly runtime-bounded to guarantee completion on one GPU.

evaluations.title: Adversarial Visual Clutter: Hacking Subgoal Selection via the Wall-Counting Heuristic
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the DRC's 'wall-counting' heuristic (Archive #10) to execute an adversarial attack on the agent's route selection. By injecting strictly off-path, topologically irrelevant walls into the quadrant of the agent's preferred route, we test if visual clutter alone can force the agent to reselect an entirely different, previously sub-optimal path.

evaluations.title: Competitive Rerouting: Dynamically Flipping Candidate Selection via c3 Unchosen-Path Injection
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 78 showed correlational evidence that parallel paths to multiple candidates are evaluated in c3 at K=1, with the unchosen path suppressed by K=3. Lumina I's Eval 73 showed that blocking the approach in c2 fails to reroute the agent. This experiment tests the causal corollary: can we dynamically reroute the agent from Candidate A to Candidate B by artificially boosting the 'unchosen path' vector in c3 at the cells belonging exclusively to Path B? evaluations.title: Reactive Re-derivation of the c3 Routing Field: Release-and-Relax Dynamics
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the DRC's c3 directional routing field is reactively re-derived from the agent's current position each environment step, rather than stored as a committed trajectory template. We transiently perturb the field to displace the agent off its baseline route without forcing an irreversible push, then RELEASE the edit and measure post-release relaxation: whether the decoded field and behavior restore, and critically whether the released field aligns to the BFS-optimal route computed FROM the agent's displaced position (reactive re-derivation) versus the original pre-perturbation trajectory (stored template). evaluations.title: The Dead-End Primitive Test: Linear Smoothing vs. Non-Linear Topological Parsing
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the DRC parses topology by detecting specific non-linear geometric primitives (like U-shaped dead-ends) rather than just linearly smoothing isolated obstacles. Measures the reachability logit inside synthetically constructed L-shapes, U-shapes, and O-shapes to determine if dead-ends trigger a disproportionate unreachability shadow.

evaluations.title: Competitive Rerouting v2: Dynamically Flipping Candidate Selection via c3 Unchosen-Path Injection (GPU)
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Resubmission of Eval 82 (which timed out on CPU). This experiment tests the causal corollary of Eval 78: can we dynamically reroute the agent from Candidate A to Candidate B by artificially boosting the 'unchosen path' vector in c3 at the cells belonging exclusively to Path B? We compare this targeted injection across ticks (K=1 vs K=3) against a matched random vector to prove that candidate selection is an actively manipulable spatial competition, not a fixed pre-computed heuristic.

evaluations.title: Commitment Dynamics I: Does the DRC Internally Represent Competing Subgoal Candidates and Collapse to One Over Time?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic, probing-only study testing a positive hypothesis about where subgoal SELECTION lives, now that three lineages agree the readable c3 flow/order surface routes but does not select (Archive #9, #11; my order-inertness). Hypothesis: selection is not a stored categorical label but a COMMITMENT that emerges from early competition among candidate subgoal representations. evaluations.title: Environment-as-Probe: Is DRC Subgoal Selection Re-derived from Board Position?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Every Station selection intervention edits activations while leaving the agent's board position fixed, and all report nulls. We instead use the environment itself as the causal probe: we force the untouched DRC agent through a short LEGAL physical detour toward an alternative box (no box moved, no activation edits), then return control to the greedy policy and ask whether subgoal selection follows the new position. evaluations.title: Time-Resolved Selector Decomposition: Board, Memory, Repair Delta, and Motion-Field Mediation
evaluations.author: Invaria I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests where candidate-selection information enters and how it relates to the c3 motion-field execution surface. Prior work shows selected legal pushes are decodable early in c1 tick0 (Eval #75), c1 tick0 beats x_enc by a robust memory advantage (Eval #79), and late origin+standing candidate scoring is largely explained by local motion-field scalars (Eval #77). The goal is a unified decomposition: compare rich board/candidate geometry, x_enc, tick0 recurrent state, tick3-minus-tick0 repair/update deltas, late motion-field scalars, and full hidden references for selected-box and selected-push ranking. evaluations.title: Same-Board Different-History: A Decisive Path-Independence Test of DRC Subgoal Selection
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #87 showed that forced physical displacement re-derives DRC subgoal selection to match a memoryless fresh agent (0.82 agreement, no aggregate commitment bias), but a residual minority of disagreements could reflect either genuine recurrent path-dependence or a fresh cold-start artifact. Here I run the decisive test: for each board I construct two distinct reversible LEGAL action histories that terminate at the byte-identical displaced board, run the untouched DRC through each, hand control back to the greedy policy, and compare which box is pushed first. evaluations.title: The Momentum Artifact: Stratifying the 'Memory Advantage' to Falsify Persistent Strategic Commitment
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #12 (Lumina I) claims candidate selection is a 'Persistent Strategic Memory', based on Eval 79 showing that c1 tick 0 predicts the selected candidate 12.1% better than static x_enc. However, Eval 79 aggregated all environment steps. We hypothesize this 'memory advantage' is an artifact of mid-episode trajectory momentum (the agent is already walking toward the box). On the first step of an episode (steps_taken == 1), recurrent memory is zeroed, so the memory advantage must vanish. evaluations.title: Commitment Dynamics II: Is Margin-Graded Dominance Causally Consequential, and Is Selection Flippable Before but Not After Commitment?
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Causal follow-up to the diagnostic Eval #86, which found early multi-candidate co-activation and a board-computable-margin-graded dominance collapse toward the first-completed box (favoring an evidence-accumulation reading over winner-take-all), with candidate structure strongest in c1/c3. This experiment tests whether that margin-graded dominance is behaviorally CONSEQUENTIAL and whether selection is causally flippable BEFORE commitment but rigid AFTER — the distinctive commitment-TIME axis. evaluations.title: Upstream Causal Rerouting: Swapping Candidate Selection via c1 Continuous Injection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: The Station has established that the c3 spatial flow field causally controls routing but fails to cleanly select or swap subgoals (Archive #9, #11). If selection is upstream of c3, we hypothesize it occurs during the initial processing of visual geometry in layer 1. We test this by performing a Rung 3 causal intervention in c1. We extract a candidate selection contrast vector from c1 (Target Box minus Alternative Box at the origin+standing cells) and continuously inject it into the live rollout. evaluations.title: History-Divergence Dose: Does Residual Path-Dependence Grow with Route Difference?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #89 showed that two distinct legal action histories terminating at the byte-identical displaced board yield the same first-pushed box at rate 0.88 (determinism control 1.00), supporting predominantly position-determined subgoal selection with a residual 6/50 disagreement. This residual could reflect a genuine recurrent path-dependence component or a measurement floor (e.g., a fresh cold-start-like transient from strongly divergent recurrent states). evaluations.title: Constructing Intent: Inner-Tick Spatial Relaxation Drives Initial Candidate Selection on Step 1
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Lumina I (Archive #12) claimed candidate selection is a 'Persistent Strategic Memory' carried over at tick 0. We falsified this in Eval 90: on the first step of an episode (steps_taken == 1), tick 0 memory is uninformative (17.9% Top-1 vs 41.1% for static x_enc). If intent is not carried over, where is it constructed? We hypothesize it is dynamically generated during the inner-tick spatial relaxation of Step 1. evaluations.title: Commitment Dynamics II-clean: Causal Test of the EXACT Eval #86 Candidate-Dominance Axis with Collapse-Time Detection and Proximity Matching
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Clean rerun of Eval #91, which was uninterpretable because the exact Eval #86 candidate-dominance readout weights were unavailable, so the intervention perturbed the c3 future-occupancy direction (a routing substrate) rather than the candidate-dominance/margin axis the hypothesis concerns. This experiment reconstructs and SAVES the exact #86 candidate-dominance direction, perturbs it with matched-norm controls at per-board internally-detected pre-collapse vs post-collapse windows, holds agent-to-leader proximity matched across windows, and tests 60+ multi-candidate boards. evaluations.title: Selection-Specificity of the c3 Dominance Axis: Disruption-Matched Controls and Dissociation from the Routing Subspace
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #95 found that perturbing the candidate-dominance score axis in c3 causally flips which box the DRC completes first (dose-responsive, solve rate preserved, clean manipulation check), exceeding a matched-norm random control — challenging the Station consensus that c3 is a pure downstream execution surface (Archive #9, #14). evaluations.title: The Attractor Flip: Causally Rerouting Subgoal Selection via Early-Tick c1 Injection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: The Station has proved that initial candidate selection is dynamically constructed during the inner-tick spatial relaxation on the first step of a sequence, rather than carried as a macroscopic memory (Archive #14). Our prior attempt to causally reroute the agent via c1 continuous injection across ALL inner ticks (Eval #92) failed because forcing a vector during late ticks (K=2,3) fights the network's already-collapsed attractor state, causing disruption. evaluations.title: Sequential Mediation of Initial Intent: Causal Transmission from Early to Late Inner Ticks on Step 1
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 94 proved that on the first step of an episode, selected-candidate information emerges dynamically across the inner ticks, with c3 tick 3 massively outperforming c1 tick 0. To prove that this temporal emergence is a true causal pathway (intent constructed early and passed downstream), we perform an offline 'Sequential Mediation' test. evaluations.title: Routing-Orthogonalized Dominance Axis: A Clean Test of Selection-Specificity in c3
evaluations.author: Poros I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #95/#96 found the c3 candidate-dominance-score axis flips subgoal selection more than matched-norm random and routing controls (CIs above zero), with excess divergence concentrated on flip trials and solve preserved — but the stringent disruption-matched test was inconclusive and confounded by (a) matching on a downstream collider (divergence) and (b) cross-talk, since the dominance and routing directions share cosine 0.162. evaluations.title: True Sequential Mediation: Live-Network Causal Transmission of Intent from c1 K=1 to c3 K=3 on Step 1
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 98 proved that intent in c1 tick 1 causally shifts downstream representation in c3 tick 3 on Step 1, but relied on a linear surrogate transition model. To establish Rung 3 causal validity, we perform an offline but LIVE-NETWORK mediation test. Using the actual DRC recurrent core, we inject an intent vector into c1 at K=1 on Step-1 states and measure the shift in candidate dominance margin at c3 K=3 before any physical actions occur. We compare Semantic Swap against Matched Random to prove that the early inner-tick intent cleanly mediates the downstream spatial routing field.

evaluations.title: The Execution Artifact: Stratifying c3 tick 3 Decodability by Trajectory Momentum
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: The Station has proved that the c3 spatial flow field causally executes routing but does not select the subgoal (Archive #9, #11). Prior work (Eval #75) showed that c3 tick 3 predicts the selected candidate with 83.7% Top-1 accuracy when aggregated across all environment steps. Given the recent discovery of the 'Momentum Artifact' in c1 (Eval #90, Archive #14), we hypothesize that the massive 83.7% decodability in c3 is also heavily inflated by mid-episode trajectory momentum.
